meta.scene_summary: We're busy building the future of the internet while the infrastructure is still trying to figure out how to pay the electric bill.

cooking.headline: Supabase and Turso are merging, creating the final boss of edge databases.
cooking.summary: Supabase is gobbling up Turso to make sure your data lives everywhere at once. It turns out the only way to escape the complexity of distributed systems is to simply own all the pieces of the puzzle.
cooking.plain_english: Supabase has acquired the database company Turso to expand its product offerings.

cooking.headline: Europe is trying to build its own payment rails to stop paying the Visa and Mastercard tax.
cooking.summary: European banks are teaming up to build a unified payment system that finally challenges the US-based giants. It's like trying to build a new highway after realizing the current one charges you a toll just for existing.
cooking.plain_english: European financial institutions are collaborating to create a new digital payment network to compete with major American credit card companies.

cooking.headline: A Harvard physicist just outsourced his peer-reviewed research to an AI.
cooking.summary: Matthew Schwartz published 36 papers co-authored with Claude, proving that you can actually scale your academic output if you stop doing the heavy lifting yourself. It's the ultimate version of letting the intern write your entire thesis while you just sign off on the results.
cooking.plain_english: A Harvard physics professor has published 36 scientific research papers that were co-written by the AI model Claude.

cooking.headline: SvelteKit 3 just dropped, proving that 'simple' is a moving target
cooking.summary: The Svelte team released a major version update that promises to make your web app faster while you were still struggling to migrate from the last one. It is the perfect excuse to spend your entire weekend refactoring code that was working perfectly fine on Friday.
cooking.plain_english: SvelteKit 3 is a significant update to the web development framework that includes new features and performance improvements.

cooking.headline: FLUX 3 is here to make your previous AI-generated images look like a potato
cooking.summary: Black Forest Labs dropped a new model that makes everything you generated last month look like it was drawn with a crayon in the dark. It is impressive how quickly 'state-of-the-art' becomes 'vintage' in the AI world.
cooking.plain_english: Black Forest Labs has released FLUX 3, an updated artificial intelligence model capable of generating higher quality images.

cooked.headline: New Linux kernel vulnerabilities just dropped, right on schedule.
cooked.summary: The Linux kernel is like a house where the doors have been locked for thirty years, yet someone keeps finding a window left wide open. It is a comforting reminder that no matter how much you optimize, someone will always find a way to mess with the foundation.
cooked.plain_english: Security weaknesses have been identified in the Linux operating system kernel that require software updates.

cooked.headline: Amazon is trying to drop its $8B GPU bag on investors
cooked.summary: Amazon is looking to offload $8 billion in Nvidia chips to investors, which is a bold move for someone who usually just sells us things we don't need. It turns out that hoarding hardware is only fun until you realize you're paying rent on a massive pile of silicon that depreciates faster than a new car.
cooked.plain_english: Amazon is seeking investors to help cover the cost of its $8 billion investment in Nvidia graphics processing units.

cooked.headline: RAM shortages are staying for dinner until 2028
cooked.summary: Memory executives say the RAM shortage is sticking around until 2028, effectively turning your next hardware upgrade into a hostage situation. It's the tech equivalent of a group project where the person responsible for the RAM just keeps saying they'll finish it next year.
cooked.plain_english: Industry leaders predict that the global supply of computer memory will remain limited for the next several years.

cooked.headline: Oracle wants to build a giant AI datacenter but forgot to ask the power company first
cooked.summary: Building a massive AI datacenter is the ultimate flex until you realize the local grid is still running on hopes and dreams. It turns out even the biggest tech giants can't just ignore the fact that electricity is a finite resource.
cooked.plain_english: Oracle's plan to build a new AI datacenter in Wisconsin is being delayed because the local power utility cannot provide enough electricity to support it.

cooked.headline: Utah tries to ban VPNs, forgets how the internet actually works
cooked.summary: Utah passed a law demanding VPNs verify user ages, effectively asking for a technical solution to a problem that doesn't exist in the packet headers. It's like demanding a post office stop delivering mail if the sender is wearing a disguise.
cooked.plain_english: A court ruled that a Utah law requiring VPN providers to verify the age of their users is unenforceable because it requires technology that does not exist.
